correctness.rationale: For each laminar group T define load minus uniform-eligibility fractional share. Children partition every parent, so a parent excess below |parent|/|original eligibility set| forces a child below the corresponding relative-size threshold. Choosing recursively yields a singleton and preserves all group excesses below one, by cases: chosen descendants increase by 1-|T|/|S|; other descendants decrease; supersets/disjoint groups unchanged. This proves the all-size statement and implies unit-chore Prop1; a single globally eligible chore gives sharpness. Python exact Fraction replay checked 50,983 finite histories and 2,198,655 group inequalities; finite tests do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The restriction that eligibility sets form a known laminar hierarchy is natural in hierarchical workforce/resource assignments. Unlike the general unrestricted online unit-chore Θ(sqrt(m)) approximation landscape, it permits exact anytime eligibility-aware Prop1 and the stronger simultaneous group upper-quota bound for every prefix and adaptive sequence; the uniform one-chore discrepancy constant is sharp across population sizes. The structural invariant is an algorithmic guarantee, not a routine reassignment of a precomputed offline fair allocation or an arbitrary small census.
